problem:
In each square of a garden shaped like a $45 \times 45$ board, there is initially a tree of height $0$. A gardener and a lumberjack alternate turns playing the following game, with the gardener taking the first turn:

\begin{itemize}
  \item The gardener chooses a square in the garden. Each tree on that square and all the surrounding squares (of which there are at most eight) then becomes one unit taller.
  \item The lumberjack then chooses four different squares on the board. Each tree of positive height on those squares then becomes one unit shorter.
\end{itemize}

Additionally, there is a magic bird that flies around the garden and sings a beautiful song every time the lumberjack chooses a square.

We say that a tree is \emph{majestic} if its height is at least $10^{6}$. Determine the largest number $K$ such that the gardener can ensure there are eventually $K$ majestic trees on the board, no matter how the lumberjack plays.
